translated_text: Even if rivers run between different states, or even if they flow between two countries, international courts and the Supreme Court of India have affirmed that the command area for irrigation has the greater right over it. The Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal and the Supreme Court have clearly stated in their rulings that any construction across the Cauvery for irrigation purposes must obtain the approval of the states of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. The impacts of the Mekedatu dam on the environment, the threats to food security, and the drinking water shortage are included. We must raise these aspects and file numerous cases successively in the Supreme Court. The Karnataka government has prepared a detailed revised project report for constructing the Mekedatu dam and submitted it to the Central Government. Accordingly, if the dam is built and completed, 12,500 acres of forest land will be converted into a reservoir area, and 12,500 acres of land belonging to the Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary will be submerged in water. Elephants, tigers, and birds will lose their habitats; as a result, rare species of animals, including wildlife, will be destroyed; many hill-dwelling villages will be submerged; this will become a major environmental disaster. Furthermore, in the reservoir areas, 890,000 trees will be cut down and felled. Although the capacity of the Mekedatu dam is said to be 67 TMC, since the reservoir area is larger, it can be filled up to more than 70 TMC. Not even a drop of water will come to Tamil Nadu. As a result, the Cauvery irrigation districts will soon become deserts. In 25 districts, 50 million people will face a lack of drinking water. Which part is in the Rasimalai region of Krishnagiri district? It is located 10 km from Biligundlu, where the Cauvery water for Tamil Nadu is measured. This place is a feasible area for building a dam to store surplus water coming to the Mettur Dam and to generate electricity. That is why Kamaraj laid the foundation for the Rasimanal Dam in 1961. Efforts for it continued even during M.G.R.'s tenure. The Rasimanal region belongs to Tamil Nadu on the left bank of the Kaveri and to Karnataka on the right bank. Since there are hills on both sides of that area, it is possible to store about 66 TMC of water. If a dam is built in the Rasimanal area, water storage areas can be created in two sections from there: upwards up to 42 km to Mekkedattu, and northwards for 25 km up to Anchetti. Compared to the Mekkedattu dam, this would have a lower cost. If a small hydroelectric power station is set up here, electricity can be generated. Drinking water can be transported from Rasimanal to Bengaluru. It is only in the Philigundulu area that water for Tamil Nadu is accounted for. The Cauvery water will be calculated here.
